title: session-entropy-benchmark-and-stability-probe
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent P99 regressions that correlate with input sequence diversity across customers. Existing workload generators focus on sequence length and concurrency but underrepresent token-level entropy and primer-to-response variability that exercise KV-cache pressure and attention kernel branching. This PR introduces a new benchmark runner and reporting pipeline to quantify 'session entropy' effects and provide a stability score that aggregates latency tail, memory jitter, and KV cache miss-rate.

What this PR adds: session-entropy-prober runner (configurable entropy profile, primer strategy, and sticky-token probability); deterministic seed-based sampler; stability-score reporter that emits CSV/JSON and a compact delta report; instrumentation hooks to tag flamepoints and KV-cache spill events; CI smoke harness for quick fidelity checks.

How to run (local): ./bin/bench run session-entropy --config=examples/entropy/profiles/high_variability.yaml --target=localhost:8080 --concurrency=32 --duration=10m --out=artifacts/entropy-high.json

Checklist: [x] runner implementation + unit tests; [x] end-to-end reporter + example profile; [x] deterministic sampling with seed option; [x] lightweight smoke CI that runs under 10m; [x] documentation snippet in README/entropy.md.

Behavioral summary: The runner supports three entropy axes: lexical diversity (vocab sample skew), structural variance (primer/template switching), and temporal stickiness (probability of token repeats within a session). Default 'stability score' is a weighted combination: 0.5*p95_latency_norm + 0.3*mem_jitter_norm + 0.2*kv_miss_rate_norm (lower is better). The reporter also computes cohort deltas between baseline and experiment and emits a small text summary for quick triage.

Why this is different from existing tools: Unlike the seq-mixer and hotpath generators, session-entropy-prober focuses on micro-level token distributions and their interaction with KV cache and attention kernel branching. It reproduces rare tail events that previously only surfaced in production traces, enabling earlier detection in CI and bench lab experiments.
commits:
4 commits:
  - a1f3e7b: add session-entropy runner core loop and sampler
  - b4c9d12: add stability-score reporter and CSV/JSON exporters
  - c2d1f98: add smoke CI job and deterministic seeding; update README with example profiles
  - e7b2a44: fix race in kv-metrics collector and add unit tests for seed determinism
review_comments: Evan Chen (review): Nice addition — please add a short explanation of the stability score weights and a pointer to how we might tune them per workload. Also prefer using the existing metrics namespace 'bench.kv' instead of 'kv_meta'.
Author reply (Priya): Switched to bench.kv and added explanation in docs/bench/entropy.md. Made weights configurable via reporter config (defaults preserved).

Marina López (review): Found a flake when running smoke on p3.2xlarge - p99 was occasionally high due to driver scheduling; request adding a retry and marking the smoke as 'best-effort' in CI metadata.
Author reply (Priya): Added retry in ci job and a 60s warmup. Also added guidance in README about isolating driver noise for GPU runs.
Daniel Foster (approval): LGTM after fixes. Verified stability_score outputs for baseline/experiment and validated reporter CSVs load into the bench ingestion pipeline.
release_notes: Add session-entropy benchmark runner and stability-score reporter. Useful for detecting tail regressions caused by token-level input diversity and KV cache pressure. Includes example profiles and CI smoke job.
